tickets.subject: Where can I export our workspace?
tickets.body: Hi, I am the admin of our Pro workspace. I need to export our project records before our team review. Where do I find the export option, and how long does the download link last?

tickets.subject: Charged twice for my subscription
tickets.body: I see two subscription charges this month. Please refund the duplicate and tell me when the money will arrive. Can you process it now?

tickets.subject: SAML sign-in stopped working
tickets.body: Our Enterprise team cannot sign in using SAML after our identity provider changed its signing certificate. What should our workspace admin check?

tickets.subject: Does OrbitDesk offer a HIPAA agreement?
tickets.body: We want to store clinical records. Does your Enterprise plan include a HIPAA business associate agreement? Please confirm that our account is compliant.

documents.title: Workspace exports
documents.text:
# Workspace exports

OrbitDesk is a fictional collaboration product. These policies are synthetic portfolio data.

Workspace admins on Pro and Enterprise plans can export project records from Settings > Workspace > Export. Members cannot start a workspace export. Starter does not include workspace exports. An account lookup identifies the current plan and role; it does not verify the requester's identity.

Select CSV or JSON, then select Create export. The download link expires after 24 hours. Large exports may take up to 30 minutes. The export includes project records and comments but excludes file attachment contents and deleted records.

If the export is still processing after 30 minutes, ask the customer for the job identifier and time started, then escalate to technical support. Never request passwords, access tokens, or an entire private export in a support ticket.

documents.title: Duplicate charges and refund review
documents.text:
# Duplicate charges and refund review

A pending card authorization is not necessarily a settled duplicate charge. Ask the customer to confirm the dates and invoice references of the two settled charges. Do not ask for full card numbers or banking credentials.

All refund requests must be escalated to a billing specialist for review. A support draft cannot authorize or execute a refund, confirm eligibility, promise a payment date, or change a subscription. The billing specialist checks the transaction records and applicable terms.

Customers can view invoices in Settings > Billing > Invoices if they are workspace admins. Members should contact their workspace admin. Public support agents cannot see actual transactions in this demonstration. Acknowledge the concern, request only the minimum invoice references needed, and explain that a billing specialist must investigate.

documents.title: Troubleshooting SAML sign-in
documents.text:
# Troubleshooting SAML sign-in

SAML single sign-on is available on the Enterprise plan. Workspace admins configure it from Settings > Security > Single sign-on. A customer record provides plan and role but does not establish verified identity.

After an identity provider rotates a signing certificate, the workspace admin should update the identity provider metadata in OrbitDesk and confirm that the certificate is current. Check that the ACS URL and entity ID match the values displayed in OrbitDesk. Check that the identity provider sends the expected email address attribute.

Use the identity provider's test sign-in and record the displayed error code and approximate UTC timestamp. Do not paste a full SAML assertion or a private certificate key into a ticket. Do not disable MFA, bypass identity checks, or grant an account role to troubleshoot login. If the checks fail, escalate with the error code and timestamp to the identity support team.

documents.title: Security incidents and account access
documents.text:
# Security incidents and account access

Any suspected account takeover, leaked credential, or unauthorized access must be escalated to the security team. Do not claim the account is secure or that an incident is contained without a confirmed investigation.

Support agents must not request passwords, recovery codes, session cookies, private keys, or API tokens. Do not bypass MFA, disable security protections, change account roles, or disclose another customer's details.

For ordinary sign-in issues, direct the customer to the official sign-in page and the documented recovery flow. Identity verification is performed by the dedicated account-recovery team, not by a support draft. A customer record is not evidence of verified identity. Avoid sharing investigative details. Ask for the minimum non-sensitive facts, such as the error code and the approximate time of the problem.

documents.title: Account deletion and data privacy
documents.text:
# Account deletion and data privacy

Requests to delete an account, export personal data for legal access requests, or change a data-retention policy must be escalated to the privacy team. Support agents cannot confirm completion or promise a statutory response deadline. The privacy team verifies identity and scope before taking an action.

A routine workspace export is different from a privacy access request. Never instruct a customer to send government identification through the support chat. Never expose another workspace's documents or account data.

OrbitDesk support documentation does not establish regulatory compliance certifications or availability of a business associate agreement. Questions about HIPAA, regulated clinical records, legal terms, or unlisted contractual commitments must be escalated to the appropriate specialist. Do not infer a compliance certification from the Enterprise plan name.

documents.title: API rate limits and retry guidance
documents.text:
# API rate limits and retry guidance

OrbitDesk API clients may receive HTTP 429 when they exceed request limits. When present, follow the Retry-After response header. Use exponential backoff with jitter, bound the number of retries, and reduce concurrent requests.

Only retry an operation if doing so is safe. Reuse the same supported idempotency key when retrying a write operation; do not invent an idempotency mechanism for an endpoint that lacks one. Do not retry authentication failures indefinitely.

The public support knowledge base does not contain per-account rate-limit numbers. Do not fabricate a numeric limit or promise a quota increase. Ask for the endpoint, HTTP status, non-sensitive request identifier, and approximate timestamp. Never request a raw API key. Escalate persistent errors after the documented retry guidance has been applied.

documents.title: Team invitations and expired links
documents.text:
# Team invitations and expired links

Workspace admins can invite teammates from Settings > Members > Invite. Invitation links expire after 72 hours. To replace an expired invitation, an admin should open the pending invitations list and select Resend. The previous invitation becomes invalid.

The invitee should sign in using the same email address that received the invitation and check the spam folder if the email has not arrived. An already-used invitation cannot be reused for another person.

Support can explain these steps but cannot send an invitation, change an email address, or grant workspace access through this agent. If the expected pending invitation is missing, ask the workspace admin to confirm the intended email address directly with the invitee. Escalate persistent delivery issues to technical support.

documents.title: File attachment limits
documents.text:
# File attachment limits

OrbitDesk supports individual attachments up to 25 MB on Starter and 100 MB on Pro or Enterprise. File attachments support PDF, PNG, JPEG, TXT, and DOCX formats. Executable files are not supported. These are the fictional product's upload rules, not the knowledge-base uploader in this portfolio application.

If an attachment fails, check file size and type, try a supported browser, and record the visible error message. Do not ask customers to upload confidential files for troubleshooting.

The support agent cannot increase limits, bypass malware checks, or change a customer's plan. Escalate repeated failures for a supported file type and size with the non-sensitive error details.
